Docs The feature card

the entity in one handle, one analogy and one constraint box

Authored in cards/progression.md — the only hand-written source on this page. Everything counted elsewhere is read from the codebase at build time.

“"The kitchen never locks a dish — it just remembers what you've practiced."”

ISthe progression engine (5 trees + NodeProgress), read-time mastery/decay/tier derivation, the skill-unlock ledger, the CookedMealCreated recompute handlers, and the Perfil/home surfaces that render them.
IS NOTthe cook loop that emits the event (cooking's card ends at the publish site) — and not the exploration BIAS preferences, which shape recipe ranking, not progression.
DECIDESwhich tree nodes a cooked meal credits, what the decayed practice count is NOW, which tier label heads the profile, and when a skill flips to learned — never which recipes a user may see or cook.

a climbing gym's chalkboard — every route you finish gets a tally under its holds (trees), tallies fade if you stop climbing (180-day decay), your grade is read off your three strongest techniques whenever someone asks (never written on you), and no route is ever roped off: climbing above your grade just writes a bigger tally.

AnalogyIn this codebase
tally per holdapps/api/models/progression.py:122-152
fading chalkapps/api/services/decay.py:19-32
grade read-offapps/api/services/mastery.py:31-51
the scan after each climbapps/api/services/progression.py:259-352
no roped-off routesSCOPE REQ-20/REQ-22

Easy to confuse:

  • the earned proficiency tier (principiante…maestro) with the PAID subscription tier — profileModel.ts:64-70 marks the icon as the rank, explicitly not the plan.
  • D-GU5's original "AVG(last 20 complexities)" — retired; the 0043 migration dropped the stored tier and the complexity handler; today's tier folds decayed technique counts.

Where the analogy stops working: the chalkboard analogy breaks at demotion — the raw signal is a high-water mark (PROG-001: cook_count never drops), so only DECAY lowers an effective count, never a recompute.

Full card — what & why, for whom, flows, is / is not

What & Why

Progression turns the cooked-meal ledger into visible growth (SCOPE SC-04/REQ-13/REQ-20) under two invariants the event bus forces. Recompute-never-increment: the bus swallows raising handlers with no retry (events/bus.py:60-87), so a += delta would silently lose meals — instead on_cooked_meal_created (services/progression.py:490-495) rescans the full dish history in one pass (_compute_kind_stats, :259-352, snapshot-over-live per field, scan cap 2000) and upserts per-node high-water marks (_upsert_node_progress, :393-434 — counts only rise; PROG-001). Derive-at-read: migration 0043 dropped the stored proficiency_tier; the profile summary (the ONLY progression endpoint — GET /profile/summary, api/profile.py:24-31) reads all NodeProgress rows, computes per-tree mastery, and heads the profile with the technique tree's tier (services/profile.py:269-300) — compute_mastery_tier averages the top-3 techniques' DECAYED counts (mastery.py:20-51; thresholds 1.5/4/8/15) where decay is a hard 180-day window (decay.py:16-32, a pure function Phase 12 can swap). Five trees exist today — technique, region, diet, ingredient, flavor — seeded from taxonomy extractors with zero authored content (progression.py:74-76, :115-188) and reconciled at deploy; the prerequisite DAG (TreeEdge) is schema-present but empty at MVP. A sibling subscriber keeps the skill ledger (services/skills.py): distinct-session counts flip attempted → learned at each skill's unlock threshold, stamping learned_at once. The whole system is reach-not-gating by construction: progression only ever WRITES node_progress; no query filters on it — an untagged manual recipe simply credits nothing, which is exactly why a cook with no technique signal floors to principiante (mastery returns None → tier_label floor, profile.py:63-70; the founder's 2026-06-23 ruling made emergent by three functions rather than a branch).

For Whom

  • The cook watching themselves grow — the Perfil's three sections (Explorar / Progreso / Estadísticas, F3) with the tier badge, per-tree level/5 bars, and recent unlocks; practice fades honestly if they stop.
  • The beginner — never blocked: any dish is cookable on day one; cooking above your level just writes a bigger tally (reach, not gating).
  • The recipe scorer — load_user_match_context reuses the SAME rows + mastery + decay to weigh the Skill lens (match_context.py:41-77), so browse and profile can never disagree about your level.
  • The maintainer — one scan per cook, pure derivation functions, and an event contract that makes a dropped handler self-heal on the next meal.

Flows

  • recompute ★ → CookedMealCreated → on_cooked_meal_created: one ledger scan → per-node high-water upserts, restricted to the cook's codes; a swallowed handler self-heals next cook. (assured: test_progression 10 + test_progression_readcutover 8 cases)
  • derive → GET /profile/summary: NodeProgress → per-tree mastery + the technique-headline tier, decayed at read time; no progression state is stored beyond the raw signal. (assured: test_profile_summary + test_profile_routes; the progression journey, 4 e2e cases)
  • unlock → the skills sibling: distinct-session counts vs skill_unlock_threshold → attempted/learned + learned_at once; home renders the 3 most recent. (assured: test_skills, 6 cases)
  • seed → deploy-time seed_progression_trees_on_startup + backfill_node_progress_on_startup: trees from taxonomy extractors (no authored content), pre-engine users backfilled from their ledger.
  • render → ProfileContainer → useProfileSummary → buildProfileDashboardViewModel; ProfileProgressSection's tree-mastery accordion (level/5 bars, "Sin práctica aún" on null); the home checklist reads techniques_mastered / distinct_ingredients_used / cuisines_explored. (assured: homeModel.test.ts 10 + ProfileScreens.sectionBreakpoint 2 + HomeActionablePanel 6 cases)

Is

  • One scan, many trees: _kind_codes extracts per-kind codes from the cooked recipe; the same pass credits technique, region, diet, ingredient, and flavor nodes.
  • High-water raw signal (PROG-001): cook_count/last_cooked_at only rise; staleness is expressed at read time by decay, never by demotion writes.
  • Pure derivation functions: decay (count, last_cooked_at, now) and mastery (rows → tier|None) are clock-parameterized and swappable without touching callers.
  • Snapshot-safe tier: the tier path reads node_progress, which recomputes from per-event snapshots — a recipe edit cannot retroactively move your tier (the live-scan stats CAN move; see RISKS).
  • Reach-not-gating by construction: the engine writes one table and filters nothing (REQ-20/REQ-22).

Is Not

  • not a gate — no tree state hides, downranks, or blocks any recipe; the always-open catalog is a SCOPE invariant the code satisfies by never joining progression into a query.
  • not the cook loop — cooking publishes; this entity subscribes.
  • not the exploration preferences — those bias recipe ranking (recipe entity); explorationModel.ts is a profile-rendered seam into that system.
  • not the country tree / character sheet — SCOPE Phase 4.1 material; no country tree kind, no focused_tree, no GET /profile/stats exists in code today.

Code Data model

DB entities and API shapes — each names its file and the endpoints that touch it

A field typed with another documented class LINKS to it (violet) instead of repeating its structure. Examples are synthetic — derived from Literal values and field-name heuristics, never real user data.
Type colors — one hue per family, deeper = the wider type: int float · Decimal numeric · date · time datetime temporal · str bytes · Text textual · bool · list · dict · Literal structured · UUID identity · None nullable. An uncolored token is a domain alias (an enum defined in this codebase).
Insight icons — the DATA-MODEL lens; the same shape runs over other member kinds later (functions · methods), scoped, never mixed:
  • model — a persisted DB entity: lives in a table, owns FKs.
  • schema — an API / pipeline shape: crosses a boundary, owns no storage.
  • base — derives from NOTHING: no FK out, no field typed by another documented class; a foundation others build on.
  • N god-class flag — field count ≥ 15; the number that makes it a split candidate below.
  • Class N% closest structural twin — % = shared fields over the union (Jaccard); a ≥80% pair becomes a merge candidate below.
  • Usage bars: teal = api (endpoint touches + FK in) · violet = internal (mapped backend files referencing the class). Both bars are EVIDENCE, never a verdict: they count references inside the config-mapped files only, so a zero means no indexed usage — go check, never dead. One unmapped file falsifies a zero; nothing falsifies a count.

About this section

Backend: services/progression.py (the engine spine — kinds, seeds, the scan, high-water upserts, the handler), services/mastery.py (tier derivation), services/decay.py (the 180-day window), services/skills.py (the unlock ledger), services/profile.py (build_profile_summary — the read-cutover tier + the live stats scan), api/profile.py (the one endpoint), services/match_context.py (the scorer's reuse of the same derivation). Data: models/progression.py (SkillTree/TreeNode/TreeEdge/NodeProgress), models/skill.py (SkillProgress); migrations 0042 (engine) + 0043 (the contract-drop). Web: features/profile/profileModel.ts (tier display + tree mastery mappers), useProfileSummary.ts, screens/ProfileScreens.tsx (the F3 three-section Perfil), components/ProfileProgressSection.tsx (the multi-tree accordion), homeModel.ts (the checklist reads), ProfileContainer.tsx.

Code Data-model candidates

MERGE and SPLIT — named by the machine, ruled by judgment; the verdict lands in DECISIONS/PENDING via review or a health pass, never here

What the candidate icons mean
  • merge — structural twins ≥ 80% (from the similarity flag).
  • split — a god class ≥ 15 fields (from the N fields flag).
Why these two, and not "nothing uses this" — similarity and size are CORPUS-COMPLETE signals: two mapped classes sharing 87% of their field names is TRUE no matter what lives outside the map, and a 22-field class is 22 fields however little the config covers. Absence of references is neither — a single file outside the entity config falsifies it. This section names only what the instrument can actually support. The usage evidence lives on the Data model page — two bars per class, api and internal — and a reader checks it there.
The floor, stated honestly — the similarity flag records the TOP-1 nearest neighbour per class only, only above the 50% line, Python only, mapped files only, and only field NAMES (types and semantics are not compared). Every one of those is a way to MISS a pair, never a way to invent one. This TABLE cuts higher still — it lists pairs at ≥ 80%, so the 50% recording floor is what the flag sees, not what you are reading. This page is a FLOOR, not a census: it under-reports duplication and always will. That direction is the safe one — under-reporting a positive signal costs you a missed merge; under-reporting absence gets live code deleted.
Known blind spot — classes outside the entity config are invisible here, and the misses cluster there rather than in the maths: two modules can carry near-identical schemas and drift apart for months without either appearing on this page, if one of them is not in the config. An empty candidates table means the mapped set is clean, not the repository.

every def in this entity's mapped backend files — the FUNCTIONS lens, sibling of the data model above

Insight icons — the FUNCTIONS lens:
  • function — a module-level def.
  • method — a def bound to a class.
  • endpoint handler — a route decorator serves it.
  • base — calls no other documented function; a foundation others build on.
  • N god-function flag — length ≥ 50 lines; makes it a split candidate below.
  • fn N% closest structural twin — body-identifier overlap (Jaccard); a ≥85% pair becomes a merge candidate below.
  • Usage bars: teal = api (endpoints served + api-layer files referencing) · violet = internal (mapped files referencing — same-file calls outside the def count: a helper used within its module is used). Both bars are EVIDENCE, never a verdict: the scan reads config-mapped Python only, so a zero reads no indexed caller — go check, never dead.

Code Function candidates

MERGE and SPLIT — named by the machine, ruled by judgment; same contract as the data-model candidates, function-scoped

What the candidate icons mean
  • merge — identifier twins ≥ 85% (from the similarity flag).
  • split — a god function ≥ 50 lines (from the N length flag).
Why these two, and not "nothing calls this" — similarity and length are CORPUS-COMPLETE signals: two mapped defs sharing 87% of their body identifiers is TRUE regardless of what lies outside the map, and a 120-line function is 120 lines however little the config covers. "Nothing references this" is falsified by one file outside the corpus — so this section names duplication and size, and never asserts deadness. The usage evidence lives on the Functions page — two bars per def, api and internal — and a reader checks it there.
The floor, stated honestly — the similarity flag records the TOP-1 nearest neighbour per def, only among defs with ≥ 8 body identifiers, only above the 60% line, Python only, mapped files only — while this TABLE cuts higher still, listing pairs at ≥ 85%. Every one of those is a way to MISS a pair, never a way to invent one. The page is a FLOOR, not a census — and that direction is the safe one: under-reporting a positive signal costs a missed merge, while under-reporting absence gets live code deleted.
Known blind spot — files outside the entity config are invisible here, and the misses cluster there rather than in the maths: two modules can share dozens of byte-identical functions and drift apart for months without either appearing on this page, if one of them is not in the config. An empty candidates table means the mapped set is clean, not the repository.
